text: US stocks gave back part of Monday's Nvidia-fueled rally on Tuesday, with the S&P 500 down 0.5% to about 7,202 and the Nasdaq down 1.5% to about 23,741, while the Dow rose 0.9% to about 50,029. Nvidia fell about 6% and chip names such as Analog Devices and Texas Instruments dropped sharply, with technology leading the declines ahead of Wednesday's PCE inflation report. The TSX closed at 33,962.25, down 0.35%, with materials, technology and financials weighing. In Europe the STOXX 600 fell about 0.7% and the FTSE 100 about 0.1%, as miners and chip stocks slid. Asian chip stocks rallied on Jensen Huang's return at Nvidia, with Taiwan's Taiex reported up about 9% and the Kospi above 5,000, though other Asian closes could not be confirmed.
mood: Profit-taking after Monday's AI and chip rebound: chip stocks reversed lower and miners fell, while the Dow and defensive sectors held up ahead of inflation data.

veqt.t: S&P 500 -0.5%, Nasdaq -1.5%, Dow +0.9%, as Nvidia fell about 6% and chip stocks reversed.
TSX fell 0.35% to 33,962.25, led lower by materials, technology and financials.
STOXX 600 -0.7% and FTSE 100 -0.1%, with miners down sharply and Sanofi up on its Insmed deal; Nikkei and DAX closes were not confirmed.
Taiex reported up about 9% and the Kospi above 5,000 on the chip rally; Hang Seng and Shanghai closes were not confirmed.

label: Slightly bearish today
